audit.whatIsWrong: This side read Vayne on five of seven stages; the already-audited Sion side set the chart to Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Sion, Skill, Vayne across both layers.
audit.why: Mirror is authority for this run. Its basis holds up: Roar of the Slayer is an 800-range slow with armour shred on 12s at rank 1, Decimating Smash knocks up, and Soul Furnace shields the trade back, so lane is not free — Vayne's edge is the two-item row.
audit.corrected: Skill, Sion, Sion, Skill, Sion, Skill, Vayne — matched full/content pairs plus the ratings that contradicted them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Vayne's stage on the strength of Final Hour; Unstoppable Onslaught is the stronger 6.
audit.why: Unstoppable Onslaught travels up to 7500 units, knocks up harder the further it has charged, and creates terrain-style zoning. Vayne has no dash outside Tumble's 300 units, so it is a retreat-cutter — Flash is the answer, not damage.
audit.corrected: His 6 beats yours; your spike is two items of Silver Bolts.
sources: kit: Unstoppable Onslaught 7500 range, terrain flag

audit.whatIsWrong: Five separate lines claim Condemn cancels or interrupts Unstoppable Onslaught. Nothing in the kit supports that, and the Sion-side audit flagged it as explicitly unverified.
audit.why: Riot's text for Unstoppable Onslaught says nothing about displacement, and the kit carries no unstoppable field either way. Shipping a cancel that may not exist is the worst kind of error — a player commits Condemn to it and dies. Replaced with what is verifiable: Condemn's terrain stun, and Glory in Death's healing meaning Grievous Wounds decides extended trades.
audit.corrected: Do not spend Condemn on his charge; use it to put him into a wall, and buy anti-heal before long fights.
sources: kit: Glory in Death heal flag
